subtopics.title: Why Two Records of One Bank Account Differ

questions.question: A deposit banked on 27 February that only clears in March is best described as:
options: A TIMING difference — correctly recorded by the business, not yet processed by the bank
An omission that must be entered in the Cash Receipts Journal
An error by the business
A dishonoured receipt

questions.question: Service fees, interest credited, stop orders and debit orders reach the bank statement before our journals because:
options: The bank invents them each month
The business did not initiate them and was not told, so they were never journalised
They are timing differences
They may only appear on the reconciliation statement

questions.question: The rule that governs the whole topic states that:
options: Every statement item is entered in the journals
No statement item is ever entered in the journals
Our omissions and our errors are corrected in our books; timing differences and the bank's errors go on the reconciliation statement
Only items above R500 are corrected

questions.question: Before any figure is written in a bank reconciliation question, each item must first be:
options: Rounded to the nearest ten rand
Deducted from the statement balance
Posted to the trial balance
Sorted into one of three boxes — timing difference, our omission, or error

questions.question: A debtor's EFT of R5 400, already recorded in the CRJ, is dishonoured. The correcting entry is:
options: Debit Debtors control, credit Bank
Debit Bad debts, credit Bank
Debit Bank, credit Debtors control
Debit Sundry expenses, credit Bank

questions.question: A payment to a creditor of R5 720 was entered in the CPJ as R5 270. The correction is:
options: Debit Bank R450, credit Creditors control R450
Debit Creditors control R450, credit Bank R450
Debit Creditors control R5 720, credit Bank R5 720
No correction — the bank must adjust its statement

questions.question: Cheque 0873 for R8 100, issued on 15 July 2025 and still unpresented at 28 February 2026, must be:
options: Carried on the outstanding list indefinitely
Written off as a bad debt
Cancelled as stale — debit Bank, credit Creditors control
Deducted from the bank statement balance

questions.question: Starting from a provisional Bank account balance of R72 540 and processing the seven February findings, the corrected balance is:
In the reconciliation statement, R2 950 debited to the business in error by the bank is:
options: ADDED to the bank statement balance, because the bank will give it back
Subtracted from the bank statement balance
Entered in the Cash Payments Journal
Ignored on both sides

questions.question: Outstanding EFTs of R11 460 and R9 840 are treated as:
options: An addition of R21 300 to the statement balance
A deduction of R21 300 from the statement balance, because the bank still has to take them off
A correction in the Cash Payments Journal
A stale-cheque cancellation

questions.question: The bank statement closes at R67 540. Adding the R19 800 outstanding deposit and the R2 950 bank error, and deducting R21 300 of outstanding EFTs, gives:
The dependable test for whether an item is added or subtracted on the reconciliation statement is:
options: Deposits are always added and payments always subtracted
Round amounts are added
Follow the order in which items appear on the statement
Ask what the BANK will still do to this balance, then follow it

subtopics.title: Traps, Method Marks and Internal Control

questions.question: Entering an outstanding deposit in the Cash Receipts Journal is wrong because:
options: It is already in our books — that is exactly why it is outstanding — so it would be recorded twice
Deposits are never journalised
The bank has already processed it
It belongs in the Cash Payments Journal

questions.question: Method marks in this topic are protected mainly by:
options: Writing only the final balance
Showing the corrected Bank account with contra accounts named, and a fully headed reconciliation statement with brackets on every subtraction
Rounding all figures to the nearest hundred
Copying the bank statement line for line

questions.question: The internal control argument for the bank reconciliation is that:
options: It lowers the bank's monthly fees
It is a legal requirement of the bank
An outside party independently records every movement of cash, so comparing records exposes theft, omission and error
It removes the need for a bookkeeper

questions.question: A deposit that keeps surfacing only after month end is the classic signature of:
options: A stale cheque
A bank error
Capitalised interest
Lapping — using a later receipt to cover an earlier theft

subtopics.title: Two People Counting the Same Money

questions.question: The savings club comparison shows that two honest records differ mainly because:
options: Two people wrote things down at two different moments — same money, two clocks
One of the record keepers is dishonest
The treasurer charges a fee
The money was never banked

questions.question: The bank statement is described as "a letter from the bank" because it lists:
options: Only the errors the business made
Everything the bank did to your money that you knew nothing about
The balance forecast for next month
The suppliers you still owe

questions.question: A customer's transfer that bounces means:
options: The bank owes the business the money
The amount becomes a discount allowed
The business was never actually paid — the customer goes straight back onto the debtors list
The original sale is cancelled

subtopics.title: The Bank's News and Your Own Mistakes

questions.question: Which pile does the R19 800 uncleared deposit belong to?
options: Things you leave alone — your book is right, the bank is simply behind
News to write into the journals
Your own slip to fix
A bank fee

questions.question: A difference that divides cleanly by nine usually means:
options: A deposit is missing
Two digits have been swapped around — a transposition
The bank charged extra interest
A cheque has gone stale

questions.question: The "bread going stale" comparison in the lesson refers to:
options: Interest that stops accruing
Bank charges rising each year
A cheque expiring after six months, so it must be cancelled and the supplier put back on the list
Stock losing value on the shelf

questions.question: The three piles a learner should sort every statement item into are:
options: Debits, credits and balances
Cash, credit and contra
Assets, expenses and income
News to journalise, your own slips to fix, and things you leave alone

subtopics.title: The Bridge Between the Two Numbers

questions.question: After all news and slips are dealt with, the two numbers being bridged are:
options: The corrected Bank account of R68 990 and the bank statement balance of R67 540
The provisional R72 540 and the statement's R67 540
The deposit of R19 800 and the transfers of R21 300
The petty cash float and the bank

questions.question: The one question that decides every add and subtract on the bridge is:
options: Is it a deposit or a payment?
What is the bank still going to do to this?
Is the amount large or small?
Which journal recorded it first?

questions.question: Why does "deposits are always added" fail as a rule?
options: Deposits are rare in practice
Banks do not record deposits
It snaps the moment a question hands you an overdraft or runs the reconciliation the other way
Deposits are omissions

questions.question: Good cash practice for a small business includes:
options: Reconciling once a year
Letting the cashier reconcile the account alone
Rolling long-outstanding items forward without question
Reconciling monthly, splitting the duties, having a partner sign it off, and chasing anything long outstanding
